findings.title: Light-theme color changed for embedded post author link
findings.body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the previous light-theme color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new code uses `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` for the light-theme branch and `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)` for the dark branch. This makes the author link much lighter in light themes and likely inverts the intended 30/70 pair, reducing readability.

findings.title: Custom message length hint appears to have swapped light/dark values
findings.body: `.custom-message-length` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The change makes the light-theme value 30% and the dark-theme value 70%, which is the opposite of the desktop modal treatment and changes the light-theme text from light gray to dark gray. This looks like an accidental swap.

findings.title: Mobile topic map heading light-theme value changed unexpectedly
findings.body: In `.topic-map h3`, the previous light-theme value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`, but the new code uses 50% for the light-theme branch. Desktop keeps the 20/80 relationship for the same kind of heading. This changes the existing light-theme appearance and reduces contrast without being required by the dark-theme fix.

findings.title: Group member name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: `.user-main .user-stream .group-member-info .name` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new code uses 50% in the light-theme branch, altering the existing light-theme contrast rather than only adding a dark-theme alternative.

findings.title: Mobile group member name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: `.user-main .user-stream .group-member-info .name` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new code uses 50% in the light-theme branch, changing the existing light-theme appearance rather than only adding a dark-theme alternative.

findings.title: Missed scale-color($primary) occurrence in category badge notification
findings.body: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` without `dark-light-choose`. Since the rest of the PR wraps comparable `scale-color($primary, ...)` calls, this occurrence will not use the intended `$secondary`-based value in dark themes.

findings.title: Notification badge may have low contrast in dark themes
findings.body: `.badge-notification` keeps `color: $secondary` while its background becomes `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)` in dark themes. Because both the text color and background are derived from the dark theme's secondary/background color, the badge text may have very low contrast and be hard to read.
